messages:
Caroline (PM): Quick sync — Q3 dedicated capacity roadmap. We need final decisions on: SKU definitions for reserved pools, autoscale policy defaults, and minimum launch criteria for GA. Can teams add concrete asks/constraints by EOD?
Ben (Eng): TL;DR: We should minimize burst obligation by default, surface a paid prewarm add-on.
Dave (Infra): Agree with Ben. Tradeoffs: prewarm reduces latency but increases idle cost. We can build 3 SKUs with distinct prewarm guarantees.
Erica (CS): Customer asks from sales: 1) strict latency 99p for chat (<=150ms p95), 2) deterministic rollover windows for billing, 3) opt-in burst credits. Mostly enterprise customers.
Frank (SRE): Operational note — eviction policies need to be explicit per SKU. If we do soft-evict with backfill, oncall needs a clear playbook.
Heidi (Finance): Pricing constraint — customers expect predictable hourly commit. We can expose three tiers: reserved-s, reserved-m, reserved-l with commit multipliers. Need unit economics model before public doc.
Caroline (PM): Proposed SKU defs (draft):
```
- Reserved-S: baseline throughput 50 req/s, no prewarm, soft-burst credits up to 2x for 10m
- Reserved-M: baseline 200 req/s, prewarm pool (2x warm nodes), guaranteed p95 SLA, soft-evict with 15m drain
- Reserved-L: baseline 1k req/s, prewarm + regional standby, hard SLA & premium support
```
Ben (Eng): Implementation notes: Reserved-M prewarm can be lazy (keep minimal vram pinned) vs full warm. Lazy reduces cost but increases cold-start tail. Need to choose.
Dave (Infra): We can implement lazy prewarm (pin model weights, lazy kernel init) in 2 sprints. Full warm (runtime processes ready) is heavier (capacity + billing implications).
Erica (CS): Customers willing to pay for full warm if latency sensitive. Suggest making full warm an add-on for Reserved-M and included in Reserved-L.
Frank (SRE): Autoscale policy defaults suggestion:
```
- scale_up: add nodes when 80% cpu or request queue > 50ms for 30s
- scale_down: remove nodes after 10m idle and below 30% cpu
- burst_mode: allow 2x for 10m then degrade to best-effort
```
Ben (Eng): We need a safe fallback chain: primary model -> cheaper quantized variant -> smaller model. Fallback order must be configurable per SKU.
Caroline (PM): Launch criteria draft for GA:
- End-to-end SLA validation with 3 customer pilots (one per tier)
- Billing integration + transparent round-trip billing docs
- Rollout playbook + oncall runbook for soft/hard evictions
- Pricing slate approved by Finance
Heidi (Finance): Will review unit economics model tomorrow. Need expected utilization bands per SKU (low/med/high).
Erica (CS): I'll line up 3 pilot customers: one gaming startup (Reserved-S), one mid-market SaaS (Reserved-M), one enterprise fintech (Reserved-L).
Ben (Eng): Flag: Reserved-L requires regional standby (cross-az). Will push infra changes to support cross-region prewarm — estimate 3 sprints.
Dave (Infra): Ops-bot: creating backlog epic for cross-region standby and prewarm implementation.
ops-bot: Epic created: INFRA-1427 "cross-region prewarm + SKU support" assigned to Dave.
Frank (SRE): Can we add observability requirements per SKU? e.g., token-level cost breakdown + per-tenant latency dashboard.
Caroline (PM): Yes — make observability non-negotiable for GA. Add to launch criteria.
Heidi (Finance): Also require clear billing window definitions for burst credits (how we meter 10m windows).
Erica (CS): For pilot acceptance we'll ask customers to sign a short SOW that specifies burst behavior and eviction anchors.
Ben (Eng): Open engineering questions: 1) default fallback chain, 2) cache sharing semantics across tenants in same pool, 3) tiered autoscale hysteresis values. I can write a short RFC if folks are ok.
Caroline (PM): Please do RFC. Target: RFC by next Wed. After that we'll lock SKUs and commit to implementation timeline.
Dave (Infra): Putting tentative timeline on board: RFC (1w) -> infra spikes (2w) -> pilot infra work (2w) -> pilot runs (2w).
Frank (SRE): Add canary rollout procedure for model fallback toggles. Don't want silent degradations.
Heidi (Finance): Once RFC lands, I'll run pricing sims against 3 utilization curves.
Caroline (PM): Action items: Ben write RFC, Dave create infra epic (done), Erica secure pilots, Heidi run pricing sims, Frank draft oncall + canary runbook. Thanks — please post quick updates here as you complete tasks. :thumbsup:
